chapters.title: Chapter One
chapters.body:
Mara found the lantern beneath a shelf of maps no living surveyor remembered drawing. Its panes were dark, yet every contour on the nearest chart leaned toward it as grass leans toward rain.

She carried it to the window. The city below was all slate roofs and winter smoke, but inside the lantern a second city flickered into being, street by impossible street.

chapters.title: Chapter Two
chapters.body:
At dawn the mapmaker returned. He set down his gloves, looked once at the lantern, and locked the shop door behind him.

There are objects, he told Mara, that do not show where you are. They show where the world expects you to go.

cover.backCopy: A map that redraws itself. A lantern that remembers roads. One apprentice must decide whether every destination deserves to be found.
